STEP: design decision for round objective (SID = hyperbolic RQ-VAE guided by training-only behaviour).
READ: task text, scope contract, experiment policy, and the three earlier rounds' rejections (poincare-frechet-successor-codebook, CURVCTRL-SID feedback curvature, BRad-RQ behaviour-ranked radial assignment, behcone-prefix-rq, succboost-geoshift, Lorentz-succprofile smoothing, TSG-SID, BRANCHCURV-MOEB).
OBSERVED: the taken positions are (a) curved codebook placement / Frechet updates, (b) curvature as a controlled schedule, (c) radial ranking by behaviour entropy, (d) cone/prefix boosting, (e) smoothing of successor profiles. None of them changes the METRIC under which the residual is matched to codes.
REASONING: I therefore pick the untouched coupling position: a per-item ANISOTROPIC hyperbolic gauge metric inside the residual quantizer. Behaviour (successor-field direction u_i and resultant concentration R_i) defines the stretch axis and stretch amount; fixed negative curvature (c=1, scale-free via tanh/artanh chart) supplies the conformal/Mobius structure. Both enter one closed-form cost used for assignment and for the Frechet codebook update, so removing either changes the core computation. Switches: beta=0 -> behaviour off; c->0 (Mobius -> subtraction, artanh -> identity) -> geometry off; both on = the mechanism. No ablation arm trained, no sweep (beta = measured resultant length in [0,1], no free constants), single run.
OPEN: none; final answer block follows.
IDEA: beh-aniso-poincare-rq
TITLE: Behaviour-anisotropic Poincare gauge metric for RQ-VAE residual assignment and codebook update
MOTIVATION: In a plain Euclidean RQ-VAE the level-1 code of an item is a generic residual direction; items that are behaviourally interchangeable as predecessors (their training successors point the same way) are not pushed to share a coarse prefix, so the generative model must spend prefix capacity on behaviour-irrelevant geometry.
NOVELTY: Prior rounds moved codebook placement (Frechet/successor means), curvature schedules, radial ranking, cones and profile smoothing. This changes the metric itself: each item carries its own anisotropic Poincare gauge whose stretch axis is the training successor direction and whose stretch magnitude is the measured successor concentration, applied inside the same closed-form distance that drives assignment and codebook update.
CHANGE: Residual quantisation is run in the unit Poincare ball with Mobius residuals and a per-item anisotropic gauge (stretch 1+beta_i along u_i), so along-successor mismatches cost more than orthogonal ones; codebooks are updated as tangent Frechet means of the resulting assignments.
SPECIFICATION: c=1 fixed (tanh/artanh chart, scale-free, no normalisation constant). Per item i from training transitions get beta_i in [0,1] and unit u_i in the tangent space at 0; if sum of counts is 0 set beta_i=0. At each RQ level l, with base point p_l in the ball and target x_i=exp0(z_i): r_l = (-p_l) (+) x_i; for each code w_k compute d_k = 2*artanh(sqrt(||(-r_l)(+)w_k||^2 + beta_i*<(-r_l)(+)w_k, uhat_l>^2)) with uhat_l = normalise(log0(exp0(u_i) (-) p_l)); assign k* = argmin_k d_k; carry p_{l+1} = p_l (+) w_{k*}. Codebook update: w_k <- exp0(mean over assigned items of log0(r_l)). Behaviour refresh once per epoch from the current item embeddings.
COST: +1 dot product per (item, level, code) triple, about +30% on the level distance kernel and <5% wall clock; no new parameters and no tuning. Per-step a

t the frozen scale: batch B items x L levels x K codes x d dims extra multiply-adds for the anisotropic term (e.g. B=1024, L=4, K=256, d=64 -> 6.7e7 flops/step, 24 steps/epoch). Behaviour refresh: |E| x d (~5e5 x 64 = 3.2e7 multiply-adds) once per epoch, i.e. under 1% of an epoch; 3000 epochs unchanged in count.
HYPOTHESIS: Aligning the quantiser metric with the successor field raises the level-1 prefix hit rate of training transitions and the Stage-3 test recall@10 above 0.065; if prefix hit rate and recall do not both move, the anisotropy is not doing any hierarchical work.
RISKS: anisotropy is too mild (beta<=1 gives at most sqrt(2) cost ratio) so codes barely move; the successor direction is noisy for tail items; Mobius residuals plus Frechet codebooks are harder to optimise and may codebook-collapse; the behaviour refresh may lag the embedding drift.
BEHAVIOR SIGNAL: Directed item-to-item transitions (training split only), summarised per item as a successor resultant direction and a successor concentration.
BEHAVIOR COMPUTATION: From Stage-2 training sequences only, count directed co-occurrences N_ij within the training window into a row-normalised p_ij; with z_j = log0(exp0 of the item input embedding), b_i = sum_j p_ij * z_j/||z_j||, beta_i = ||b_i|| in [0,1], u_i = b_i/||b_i||; recomputed once per epoch from the current item embeddings, frozen within the epoch; beta_i = 0 for items with no training successors.
LEAKAGE BOUNDARY: N_ij is built exclusively from Stage-2 training split sequences before Stage-3; item ids are frozen and no validation or test interaction is read; the behaviour table is a static per-epoch refresh of training counts so no val/test item or transition can enter the SID construction.
HYPERBOLIC OPERATOR: Fixed negative curvature c = 1: Mobius addition (+), tanh/artanh exponential and logarithmic maps at the origin, Poincare distance d(x,y)=2*artanh||(-x)(+)y||, extended by the anisotropic gauge q(delta)=||delta||^2 + beta*<delta,uhat>^2, d_aniso = 2*artanh(sqrt(q)).
HYPERBOLIC LOCATION: Inside the residual quantiser of every RQ level, in both the assignment step (distance to codes) and the codebook update (tangent Frechet mean of assigned residuals).
COUPLING PATH: Training transitions -> (beta_i, u_i) -> anisotropic curved cost used to pick the code at level l -> the assigned residual whose tangent mean becomes codebook entry w_k^{l} -> the level-(l+1) base point -> the emitted SID. Removing beta removes the behaviour term from the same cost; flattening c removes the Mobius/artanh structure from the same cost; both change which code is chosen and therefore the codebooks and SIDs.
COUPLING EQUATION: d_{i,k}^{(l)} = 2*artanh( sqrt( ||(-r_l)(+)w_k||_c^2 + beta_i * < (-r_l)(+)w_k , uhat_l >^2 ) ), beta_i = || sum_j p_ij * zhat_j ||, uhat_l = normalise(log0(exp0(u_i)(-)p_l)); beta_i is the behaviour term, the Mobius/artanh curvature-c terms are the curved terms.
OBSERVABLES: code assignment histograms and codebook usage per level; level-1 and level-2 prefix hit rate of training transitions (diagnostic, recorded not gated); drift of SIDs for items whose successor field is coherent versus diffuse; RQ reconstruction error per level; Stage-3 test recall@10 as the judgement.
ABLATION BEHAVIOR OFF: beta_i set to 0 for every item, everything else identical (plain isotropic Poincare RQ); implemented behind a config flag, not trained this round.
ABLATION GEOMETRY OFF: c -> 0 limit, i.e. (-r)(+)w replaced by plain subtrac

tion, artanh(sqrt(c*q))*2/sqrt(c) replaced by 2*sqrt(||x-y||^2 + beta*<x-y,uhat>^2), Frechet update replaced by plain mean; implemented behind a config flag, not trained this round.
ABLATION BOTH ON: the full mechanism as specified (beta from training transitions plus curvature c=1 Mobius gauge in assignment and codebook update); this is the single run of the round.
SPEC EQUATIONS: exp0(v)=tanh(||v||)*v/||v||; log0(x)=artanh(||x||)*x/||x||; a(+)b=((1+2<a,b>+||b||^2)a+(1-||a||^2)b)/(1+2<a,b>+||a||^2||b||^2); p_0=0; for l in 1..L: r=(-p)(+)x; for k: delta_k=(-r)(+)w_k; q_k=||delta_k||^2+beta_i*<delta_k,uhat>^2; d_k=2*artanh(min(sqrt(q_k),1-1e-6)); k*=argmin; p=p(+)w_{k*}; SID_i[l]=k*; w_k<-exp0(sum_assigned log0(r)/count_k).
SPEC INPUTS OUTPUTS: Inputs: item embedding z_i (encoder output), per-item (beta_i,u_i) from the training transition table, current level codebooks in the ball, level base point p_l. Outputs: per-level code indices (the SID), the quantised point p_L in the ball, updated codebooks, and the standard commitment/reconstruction losses computed in tangent space.
SAFEGUARDS: clamp ||x|| to <= 1-1e-5 before log0/artanh; clamp the artanh argument to 1-1e-6 and use a safe artanh with finite gradient; clamp the Mobius denominator (1+2<a,b>+||a||^2||b||^2) to >= 1e-8; guarantee beta in [0,1] by construction (mean of unit vectors) and set beta=0, u=0 when ||b_i||<1e-8 (cold items); nan_to_num on the codebook Frechet mean and skip updates for empty codes (keep the previous entry); decay any code unused for an epoch is not tuned, the entry is simply frozen rather than reassigned.
END IDEA
